messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Siloed GPU requirements + next steps (post-demo)

Hi Sophia / Alex —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick post-call summary and the proposed next steps so we all have the same picture. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you shared
- Cross-tenant data isolation is a hard requirement (PHI flows in some inference paths).
- Unpredictable burst traffic during nightly batch enrichment windows creates cost/latency spikes.
- Need predictable p95 latency for real-time features; current infra sometimes spikes to several hundred ms.

Primary goals
- Dedicated, isolated GPU pool for the customer-facing models (no noisy neighbor risk).
- Target p95 inference latency <= 250ms for typical 8k token sequences; spike-handling up to 8000 tokens needs validation.
- Procurement-friendly commercial options: committed capacity + burst buffer.

Technical details I captured
- Model family: large transformer (~65–70B), currently running as quantized FP16/INT8 in your stack.
- Expected steady concurrency: ~50 concurrent requests; bursts up to ~200 qps for short windows (5–15 minutes).
- Region preference: us-west (GCP us-west2) for lowest latency to your customers.
- KMS integration and audit logs required for PHI-handling endpoints.

Attachments: medalign-sla-draft-v1.pdf (draft SLA outline), isolation-diagram.png (proposed tenant segmentation)

Concrete next steps / owners
- MedAlign (Sophia / Alex): confirm burst profile (avg burst frequency per week) and procurement timeline / PO cadence. Reply requested by Tue 2026-12-15.
- Redwood (Tessa / Ben): send 2 commercial options (3-month test commit and 12-month reserved pool) + ops runbook draft by Mon 2026-12-14.
- Redwood SRE (Irene): prepare isolation design notes and KMS integration checklist for legal/security teams (ETA 2026-12-20).

Questions for you now
1) Are we aligned on the 250ms p95 target as the initial SLO (you mentioned 200ms in the call — please confirm).
2) Do you need air-gapped/on-prem options, or is VPC-private hosted acceptable?
3) Who should be the procurement point-of-contact (and legal) so we can route the SLA/PO?

If that looks right I’ll get the commercial options and a short ops runbook over to you Monday. Happy to set up a technical deep-dive with Irene and our SREs next week.

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0187
tessa@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Siloed GPU requirements + next steps (post-demo)

Tessa —

Appreciate the clear write-up. A few quick clarifications from our side:

- Our internal target is actually p95 <= 200ms for the most latency-sensitive endpoints (we can accept a relaxed target for less critical jobs). Please propose both the 200ms and 250ms SLOs in your options.
- Model is Llama2-70B (we’re running it quantized to int8 for inference).
- Current steady concurrency is ~50; bursts are not daily but happen 2–3x/week for short periods (typically 5–10 minutes). Bursts can reach ~180–220 qps.
- KMS: must integrate with our AWS KMS tenant; keys are customer-managed. Also need proof points for zero cross-tenant access (SOC2 evidence or similar).

Procurement: I’m looping procurement so they can coordinate the PO timeline. Our target is to have a procurement decision by end of December, ideally signing a short pilot PO first.

Let us know when you can share the draft cost options and if a 30–45 minute follow-up on Monday/Tuesday next week makes sense to go over the SLA language.

Thanks,
Sophia Ramirez
Head of ML Ops | MedAlign
Sophia.Ramirez@medalign.com

Hi Sophia / Alex —

Thanks for the quick clarifications — helpful. Following up with a concise set of commercial/ops options we believe will address your isolation and SLO needs.

Proposed options (high level)
1) Pilot reserved pool (30-day trial)
   - 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved (isolated pool)
   - Throughput: ~200 qps burst headroom with continuous batching
   - Pricing: $X/hour (pilot discount applied), single PO for 30 days
   - SLO: configurable to 200ms p95 for supported sequence lengths; degradation policy documented

2) Standard committed capacity (12-month)
   - 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs, dedicated tenant slice (network-level isolation + KMS integration)
   - Priority routing and burst buffer (additional spot-backed GPUs for short windows)
   - Pricing: reduced hourly, committed monthly invoice + annual discount
   - SLA: 99.9% availability; latency SLO at 250ms p95 for typical traffic; optional 200ms p95 add-on

3) Enterprise isolated enclave (VPC-private/on-prem option)
   - Full customer-managed key integration (HSM/KMS), air-gapped deployment option if required
   - Custom runbook and compliance package (SOC2 artifacts, audit logs retention, per-token audit tracing)
   - Pricing: quoted per-deployment + support retainer

Operational notes
- We’ll deliver a short ops runbook that covers: model onboarding, KV cache management, autoscaling policies, fallback routing, and outage playbook. 
- KMS: We support customer-managed AWS KMS keys; our security team will provide an integration spec (we’ll include the spec in the runbook).
- Isolation: network- and process-level isolation plus tenant keying for model artifacts. We will include a short isolation-diagram.png in the package.

Next steps / timeline
- Redwood to send: line-item pricing for the three options + formal pilot PO template by Mon 2026-12-14 (attached).
- MedAlign to confirm: preferred SLO (200ms vs 250ms) and procurement owner by Tue 2026-12-15.
- Schedule a 45-minute technical review (Irene + SRE) week of Dec 16 — propose Wed 2026-12-17 10:00am PT (please confirm).

Attachments included: medalign-sla-draft-v1.pdf, isolation-diagram.png

If that works I’ll get our ops and pricing teams to convert this into formal docs.

Best,
